title: Counit-normalized constant and evaluation models of adic pullback
statement: The canonical ordinary and strict-tower derived pullback pairs admit unique counit-normalized constant-tower and evaluation comparisons. Their finite-reduction comparison retains the given quotient presentation.

proof.text: The completed coefficient projections are jointly monic, so both presentations equal the published map. For finite quotient naturality, pass through the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction and sheafification adjunction: naturality of toSheafify on the constant presheaf gives the square. proof.text: After identifying coefficient maps, both pullback constructions are literally the same balanced-tensor functor. Its identity natural isomorphism gives the module and strict-tower identifications. proof.text: Transport the published constant comparison along the unique comparisons s:L→L₀ and t:T→T₀. The complex counit formula commutes with s and t. Naturality of t at the exact constant-functor comparison and cancellation of the isomorphisms identify the generalized normalization with the published one; the published unique normalization therefore gives both existence and uniqueness.

proof.text: For evaluation, resolve the whole tower by applying the functorial flat resolution to its associated functor, then transpose back to a complex of towers. Evaluation of the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism at every level, and the tensor-K-flat resolution implies acyclic-tensor K-flatness by applying it to 0→Z for acyclic Z. Precomposition with these resolving representatives is fully faithful. The tower counit followed by evaluation and the evaluation followed by the ordinary counit give natural transformations to the same ordinary complex pullback, using the degreewise identity of evaluation and levelwise pullback. Both are invertible on resolving objects by the canonical pairs and counit transport. Their quotient descends uniquely through fully faithful precomposition, yielding exactly the required normalized evaluation comparison.
